meta.name: Sourdough Cheddar Bay Biscuits
meta.description: Red Lobster's iconic garlic-cheddar drop biscuits adapted for sourdough. 130g discard replaces most of the buttermilk, adding tang and tenderness while baking powder and baking soda handle the rise. Sharp cheddar at 68% baker's percentage, finished with a non-negotiable garlic herb butter brush.

ingredients.name: All-Purpose Flour
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Cross-source consensus, adjusted -30g for discard compensation
ingredients.rationale: Standard 250g base minus 50g flour equivalent from 130g discard (100% hydration). Verified against 14 sourdough biscuit recipes.

ingredients.name: Sourdough Discard (100% hydration, cold)
ingredients.sourcedFrom: 14 sourdough adaptation recipes, sweet spot analysis
ingredients.rationale: 100-150g is the sweet spot — enough for tang and tenderness without dominating structure. Works interchangeably with active starter at same weight.

ingredients.name: Cold Buttermilk
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Adjusted from standard 240ml, compensating for discard liquid
ingredients.rationale: Reduced from 240ml to 150ml — discard contributes ~65g liquid. Buttermilk adds fat, tang, and tenderizes gluten.

ingredients.name: Cold Unsalted Butter
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Unanimous across 10+ conventional copycats — 115g dough, 45g brush
ingredients.rationale: 115g cold butter in dough creates flaky pockets via steam. 45g melted for the signature garlic butter brush.

ingredients.name: Sharp Cheddar (block, hand-shredded)
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Stella Parks (67% ratio), cross-source range 100-170g
ingredients.rationale: 150g = 68% baker's percentage. Aggressive but supported by Stella Parks' testing. Block cheese only — pre-shredded anti-caking starch ruins melt.

ingredients.name: Baking Powder (aluminum-free)
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Universal across all 60+ sources — 1 Tbsp per ~240g flour
ingredients.rationale: Double-acting provides reliable rise. Aluminum-free (Rumford) avoids metallic aftertaste in simple baked goods.

ingredients.name: Baking Soda
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Majority of refined copycats + all sourdough versions
ingredients.rationale: Reacts with sourdough acid and buttermilk for extra lift + browning. Also neutralizes excess tang from discard.

ingredients.name: Garlic Powder
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Official Red Lobster seasoning packet + copycat consensus
ingredients.rationale: Garlic powder in dough for even distribution. Garlic powder in brush for signature flavor hit.

ingredients.name: Onion Powder
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Official Red Lobster seasoning packet, Weissman, Plum Branch Home
ingredients.rationale: Present in official mix but absent from many copycats. Adds background aromatic depth without competing with garlic.

ingredients.name: Granulated Sugar
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Majority of copycats use 1-2 tsp
ingredients.rationale: Promotes browning via Maillard reaction. Balances garlic and salt. Present in official mix as dextrose.

ingredients.name: Kosher Salt
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Cross-source range 4-8g, adjusted for baking soda sodium
ingredients.rationale: Lower end of range since baking soda contributes sodium. Garlic butter brush gets a pinch (unmeasured).

ingredients.name: Cayenne Pepper
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Sweet Cayenne, Damn Delicious, Cozy Cook
ingredients.rationale: Subtle warmth without identifiable heat. About 1/8 tsp — detectable only as background complexity.

ingredients.name: Fresh Italian Parsley (finely chopped)
ingredients.sourcedFrom: Universal in garlic butter brush across all sources
ingredients.rationale: Fresh flat-leaf for flavor in the brush. Dried parsley is mostly visual — fresh makes a real difference in the butter.

states.title: Preheat & Gather
states.direction: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C). Line baking sheet with parchment paper. Gather all vessels, equipment, and ingredients. Weigh everything out.
states.exit_condition: Oven preheating, baking sheet lined, all ingredients weighed and ready

notes.text: Use sourdough discard straight from the fridge — cold discard keeps butter from melting prematurely in the dough
Active starter works interchangeably at the same weight — slightly less tang, marginally more leavening activity (negligible in quick-bake format)

states.title: Shred Cheese
states.direction: Shred 150g sharp cheddar on the large holes of a box grater. Return shredded cheese to the refrigerator until needed.
states.exit_condition: 150g cheddar shredded on large holes, refrigerated

notes.text: NEVER use pre-shredded cheese — the anti-caking starch (cellulose, potato starch) prevents smooth melting and dries out the dough. Block cheese only.
Large-hole shreds create visible cheese pockets in every bite. Fine shreds disappear into the crumb.

states.title: Whisk Dry Ingredients
states.direction: In the large mixing bowl (V1), whisk together 220g flour, 14g baking powder, 8g sugar, 6g garlic powder, 3g onion powder, 5g salt, and 0.3g cayenne.
states.exit_condition: Dry ingredients evenly combined, no visible clumps of spices or leavener

states.title: Cut In Cold Butter
states.direction: Cut 115g cold butter into 1 cm cubes. Add to dry ingredients. Using a pastry cutter, work butter into flour until pieces are pea-sized with some larger flakes remaining. Alternatively, grate frozen butter on box grater directly into flour mixture and toss to coat.
states.exit_condition: Butter pieces are pea-sized with some larger flakes, evenly distributed through flour

notes.text: Cold butter is essential — it creates steam pockets during baking for a flaky, tender interior. Melted butter produces flat, tough biscuits (Milk Street testing confirmed).
The grated-from-frozen method is faster and produces excellent results — the thin butter shreds distribute evenly and melt into flaky layers.

states.title: Add Cheese
states.direction: Add cold shredded cheddar to the flour-butter mixture. Toss gently with a fork to coat cheese shreds in flour.
states.exit_condition: Cheese evenly distributed and coated in flour — no clumps of bare cheese

notes.text: Flour coating prevents cheese from clumping and helps it distribute evenly through the biscuits.

states.title: Combine Wet Ingredients
states.direction: In a small bowl or liquid measure (V2), stir together 130g cold sourdough discard and 150g cold buttermilk. Add 3g baking soda and stir briefly — mixture will fizz slightly.
states.exit_condition: Wet ingredients combined, baking soda dissolved and fizzing slightly

notes.text: Add baking soda LAST and bake immediately — it reacts with the sourdough acid on contact. CO2 production starts immediately and you need to get the dough into the oven before it escapes.
The baking soda serves dual purpose: extra leavening lift AND neutralizes excess sourdough tang so biscuits aren't too sour.

states.title: Fold Dough Together
states.direction: Pour wet ingredients into the dry mixture. Using a rubber spatula, fold until just combined — stop as soon as no dry flour remains. Dough should be wet, shaggy, and lumpy. Do NOT overmix.
states.exit_condition: Wet, shaggy dough with no dry flour visible. Lumps are expected and desirable.

notes.text: Overmixing is the #1 cause of dense, tough biscuits. Mix less than you think — lumpy is perfect. The sourdough acid is already weakening gluten; overmixing will make them gummy.

reminders.prompt: Rate dough consistency — should be wet and shaggy

states.title: Scoop Biscuits
states.direction: Using a 1/4 cup measure or cookie scoop, drop dough portions onto the parchment-lined baking sheet (V3), spacing about 5 cm apart. Do not press down or smooth — ragged tops bake into crispy edges.
states.exit_condition: ~10 biscuit mounds on baking sheet, evenly spaced, rough and craggy on top

notes.text: Drop biscuit format is authentic to the original Red Lobster style — no rolling, no cutting. The irregular surface creates those signature crispy edges.

states.title: Bake
states.direction: Bake at 425°F (220°C) for 12-15 minutes until tops are golden brown. Internal temperature should read 200-205°F (93-96°C) when done.
states.exit_condition: Golden brown tops, firm to the touch with slight springback, internal temperature 200-205°F (93-96°C)

notes.text: Start checking at 12 minutes — cheese adds moisture and fat that can make centers seem underdone even when exterior looks golden.

reminders.prompt: Record internal temperature of center biscuit

states.title: Make Garlic Herb Butter
states.direction: While biscuits bake, melt 45g butter in a small saucepan or microwave (V4). Stir in 1.5g garlic powder, 4g finely chopped fresh parsley, and a pinch of salt.
states.exit_condition: Garlic herb butter melted and combined, parsley evenly distributed, ready for brushing

notes.text: This garlic butter brush is the single most important element of Cheddar Bay Biscuits — it IS the signature flavor. Every source agrees: do not skip this step.

states.title: Brush with Garlic Herb Butter
states.direction: As soon as biscuits come out of the oven, immediately brush garlic herb butter generously over each hot biscuit using a pastry brush. The heat draws butter into the biscuit.
states.exit_condition: All biscuits glistening with garlic herb butter, butter visibly absorbed into the surface. Serve warm.

notes.text: Brush IMMEDIATELY while biscuits are screaming hot — the residual heat absorbs the butter and garlic into the crust. This is why Red Lobster has a dedicated biscuit person on busy nights.

sources.name: Red Lobster At Home (official box mix)

techniques.name: Sourdough discard as partial buttermilk replacement
techniques.rationale: Discard has similar pH and viscosity to buttermilk. 130g discard replaces ~65ml buttermilk + contributes 65g flour equivalent.

techniques.name: Chemical leaveners alongside sourdough
techniques.sourcedFrom: All 14 sourdough biscuit recipes, Summit Sourdough (acid-soda chemistry)
techniques.rationale: Sourdough wild yeast cannot meaningfully leaven quick biscuits. Baking powder provides double-acting rise; baking soda reacts with discard acid for bonus lift and browning.

techniques.name: Cold butter cut-in method
techniques.sourcedFrom: Milk Street (frozen butter testing), Live Well Bake Often, Once Upon a Chef
techniques.rationale: Cold/frozen butter creates discrete pieces that generate steam pockets during baking. Milk Street testing showed frozen > cold > melted for rise and flakiness.

techniques.name: High cheese ratio (68% baker's percentage)
techniques.sourcedFrom: Stella Parks/Serious Eats (67%), cross-source range analysis
techniques.rationale: 150g cheese to 220g flour. Aggressive but within tested range. Sharp cheddar shredded on large holes for visible pockets.

techniques.name: Garlic herb butter brush (post-bake)
techniques.sourcedFrom: Universal across all 60+ sources, official Red Lobster product
techniques.rationale: The defining flavor of Cheddar Bay Biscuits. Applied immediately on hot biscuits so butter absorbs into the crust.

techniques.name: Baking soda added to wet ingredients last
techniques.sourcedFrom: Summit Sourdough, food science agent analysis
techniques.rationale: Baking soda reacts immediately with sourdough acid — must bake quickly to trap CO2. Adding last minimizes gas loss.

research.strategy: 7-agent parallel research: copycat cross-reference, sourdough adaptations, official/product sources, community intel (Reddit/forums), biscuit science, premium recipe developers, ingredient sourcing (HEB)

methods.detail: 350°F (175°C) for 5-8 minutes. Best results — restores exterior crispness while keeping interior fluffy.
15-20 seconds per biscuit. Quick but softens the exterior. Cover with damp paper towel to prevent drying.
Room temperature in airtight container up to 2 days. Freeze individually wrapped up to 2 months — bake from frozen at 350°F (175°C) for 10-12 minutes.
